fred.name: Weekly Economic Index
fred.producer: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
fred.description: A weekly high-frequency gauge of real U.S. economic activity, expressed in units comparable to four-quarter GDP growth.
fred.why_it_matters: It gives a faster read on broad activity than most monthly macro releases; higher readings generally indicate stronger growth.
fred.caveat: It is a composite indicator and can revise as underlying inputs are updated.

fred.name: Chicago Fed NFCI
fred.description: A weekly composite of U.S. money-market, debt, equity, banking, and shadow-banking financial conditions.
fred.why_it_matters: Positive values indicate tighter-than-average financial conditions; negative values indicate looser-than-average conditions.
fred.caveat: Because it aggregates many markets, individual components can occasionally move in conflicting directions.

fred.name: Chicago Fed ANFCI
fred.description: The NFCI adjusted for prevailing economic conditions.
fred.why_it_matters: It helps distinguish financial tightening or easing from what would normally accompany the current economic environment.
fred.caveat: The adjustment is model-based, so it is best read alongside the unadjusted NFCI.

fred.name: Initial Jobless Claims
fred.description: Seasonally adjusted weekly first-time claims for unemployment insurance.
fred.why_it_matters: It is one of the fastest direct readings on labor-market deterioration; sustained increases are more important than one noisy week.
fred.caveat: Weekly claims are volatile and can be distorted by holidays, weather, strikes, and seasonal-adjustment effects.

fred.name: Insured Unemployment Rate
fred.description: The share of covered employment receiving unemployment insurance after an initial claim.
fred.why_it_matters: It provides a compact measure of how persistent unemployment is within the insured workforce.
fred.caveat: It covers the unemployment-insurance system rather than the entire labor force.

fred.name: Continuing Claims
fred.why_it_matters: Rising continuing claims can signal that displaced workers are taking longer to find new jobs.
fred.caveat: Eligibility rules and benefit duration mean it does not capture every unemployed worker.

fred.name: 10Y minus 3M Treasury Spread
fred.producer: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / U.S. Treasury market
fred.description: The difference between 10-year and 3-month U.S. Treasury yields.
fred.why_it_matters: A deeply negative spread is a classic signal of restrictive policy and has historically preceded U.S. recessions, although timing varies widely.
fred.caveat: The curve is a risk signal, not a deterministic recession timer, and can normalize well before economic weakness arrives.

fred.name: 10Y minus 2Y Treasury Spread
fred.producer: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / U.S. Treasury market
fred.description: The difference between 10-year and 2-year U.S. Treasury yields.
fred.why_it_matters: It is a widely followed market measure of the yield-curve slope and the expected policy/growth path.
fred.caveat: Like other curve measures, it is sensitive to term premia and is not a standalone recession forecast.

fred.name: St. Louis Financial Stress Index
fred.producer: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
fred.description: A weekly composite measure of stress across U.S. financial markets.
fred.why_it_matters: Higher readings indicate greater financial stress and can reveal tightening before it is obvious in slower economic data.
fred.caveat: Market shocks can create sharp temporary spikes that do not necessarily become persistent macro stress.

fred.name: 5-Year Real Treasury Yield
fred.description: The market-implied real yield on a five-year inflation-indexed Treasury security.
fred.why_it_matters: Real yields are an important component of the discount rate facing households, businesses, and financial assets.
fred.caveat: Real yields reflect growth, policy, term-premium, and market technicals, so higher is not mechanically bearish in every regime.

fred.name: 5-Year Breakeven Inflation Rate
fred.description: The difference between nominal and inflation-indexed five-year Treasury yields.
fred.why_it_matters: It provides a timely market-based read on inflation compensation over the next five years.
fred.caveat: Breakevens include inflation-risk and liquidity premia and therefore are not a pure measure of expected inflation.

external.name: TSA Passenger Throughput
external.description: Daily counts of travelers screened at U.S. airport security checkpoints, normalized here to a weekly average.
external.why_it_matters: It is a direct, high-frequency read on travel activity and discretionary services demand.
external.caveat: Strong seasonality, holidays, weather, and calendar effects can dominate short-run changes.

external.name: Indeed US Job Postings
external.description: A seasonally adjusted index of U.S. job postings on Indeed, with February 1, 2020 equal to 100.
external.why_it_matters: Job postings can turn before payrolls and provide a direct read on employers' hiring demand.
external.caveat: The series reflects Indeed's platform mix and methodology and may be historically revised when the methodology changes.
